description.text: Gherardo Caccianemici dal Orso, later Pope Lucius II, rose from a canon of the Basilica di San Frediano in Bologna to the papacy in March 1144.  After serving as a cardinal priest and papal legate in Germany, he was elected pope and consecrated on 12 March 1144, taking the name Lucius in honour of the earlier pontiff.

His brief pontificate was dominated by the turmoil of the Roman Commune and the struggle for control of Rome.  He negotiated a seven‑year truce with King Roger II of Sicily, fought the Senate led by Giordano Pierleoni, and ultimately died from injuries sustained in a clash with the rebels on 15 February 1145.

curiosities.text: During his reign he presented the church with a copy of the Gospels bound in gold plates and adorned with jewels, as well as silver‑gilt ampullae for use at Mass.
He accepted feudal homage from King Afonso I of Portugal on 1 May 1144, but did not recognise him as king, instead calling him Dux Portugallensis.
Lucius II was mortally wounded by a thrown stone during a battle against the Roman Senate, and died at San Gregorio Magno al Celio.
